sources.title: The Colonic Crypt: Cellular Dynamics and Signaling Pathways in Homeostasis and Cancer
sources.locator: WNT falls up the crypt axis; stem cells high WNT; WNT from base mesenchyme; differentiation completes at top; Frizzled with LRP5/6; APC/AXIN/CK1A/GSK3B complex marks beta-catenin for proteasomal degradation, membrane-recruited on WNT binding; targets c-MYC, LGR5, cyclin D1; 93% of CRC mutated, mostly APC; renewal 3-5 days. 4.5 NOTCH in SC niche and TA compartment, Delta-like/Jagged, HES1 represses ATOH1. 4.7 BMP top-high, inverse to WNT, Noggin/Gremlin at base. 4 WNT/Notch/BMP/FGF interplay.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the direction and source of the crypt Wnt gradient, the identity of the receptor complex, the composition and action of the destruction complex, the consequence of Wnt binding, the named transcriptional targets, the pathway mutation frequency in colorectal cancer, and the renewal intervals. A later addition to this pack draws four further facts from it, all from section 4: that Notch signalling is active in the stem cell niche and transit-amplifying compartment and is activated by Delta-like and Jagged ligands on adjacent cells; that HES1 represses ATOH1 and so promotes the absorptive colonocyte fate while inhibiting goblet, enteroendocrine and tuft differentiation; that BMP signalling is highest at the crypt top and decreases towards the base, inverse to WNT, a gradient maintained by the antagonists Noggin and Gremlin secreted by mesenchymal cells at the base; and the review's summary statement that coordinated interplay of WNT, Notch, BMP and FGF signalling maintains colonic epithelial homeostasis. No wording, figure, schematic, table, dataset, or example from the review was copied or adapted; the pathway walkthrough, the diagram, the arithmetic and every teaching task are this lesson's own. The review lists Dishevelled among the destruction complex components; this lesson deliberately does not repeat that placement and says so in the scene where the complex is introduced. The review also carries a swapped pair of labels in section 2.1, where colonocytes are called secretory; this pack uses section 4.5, which states the assignment correctly, and does not reproduce the error.

sources.title: Beyond the French Flag Model: Exploiting Spatial and Gene Regulatory Interactions for Positional Information
sources.locator: A morphogen gradient described as a chemical coordinate system with genes activating at different thresholds; the position-to-cue mapping can be noisy or ambiguous; one gene reading a threshold with a monotonous response function achieves at most one bit, distinguishing two regions; the four primary gap genes are estimated at 4.2 plus or minus 0.05 bits, placing a nucleus to roughly 1 per cent precision; cells need gene interaction and spatial coupling, not thresholds alone.

sources.title: Fundamental Limits to Position Determination by Concentration Gradients
sources.locator: Positional width scales as averaging time to the power minus one half, so precision improves with the square root of averaging duration; averaging about a minute can give excellent precision with only a few hundred protein copies; two-gradient systems scale more slowly at minus one quarter; biochemical noise strongly constrains subcellular positioning. The models treat positioning inside a single cell.
sources.license: CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution License permitting unrestricted use, distribution and reproduction with credit); facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the square-root scaling of positional precision with averaging time and the statement about a minute of averaging with a few hundred protein copies. The consequence that halving positional uncertainty costs four times the averaging time is this lesson's arithmetic on the source's scaling law.

sources.version: Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition; NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK26813

sources.title: Signals and Receptors
sources.publisher: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
sources.locator: Families: single-span kinase-associated, seven-transmembrane, intracellular. RTKs activated by ligand dimerization and trans-autophosphorylation creating SH2/PTB docking sites; internalised RTKs stay active in endosomes, then dephosphorylate and recycle. GPCRs share seven TM helices; GRKs phosphorylate only occupied receptor, arrestin blocks G protein and drives endocytosis. Notch is single-pass, contact-triggered; ADAM and gamma-secretase free its ICD. Nuclear receptors need no cascade.

sources.title: Ionotropic and metabotropic mechanisms in chemoreception: 'chance or design'?
sources.locator: Ionotropic and metabotropic signalling differ fundamentally in temporal properties: ionotropic is usually faster, on a millisecond to sub-millisecond timescale, because ligand binding directly gates the ion channel, while metabotropic receptors have a longer latency of a few tens to several hundred milliseconds because second messengers must be made and secondary effectors activated; metabotropic signalling then lasts longer, seconds to minutes. Insect and mammalian chemosensation.
sources.license: Copyright 2010 European Molecular Biology Organization; no Creative Commons licence on the article page; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

No wording, figure, table or example was copied or adapted. The lesson states in the scene that the comparison was established in chemosensory systems, keeps the latency and the duration as the two separate quantities the source makes them instead of merging them into one speed, and does not extend the figures to receptor tyrosine kinases or intracellular receptors, on which this source reports nothing.

sources.title: Frizzled receptors: gatekeepers of Wnt signaling in development and disease
sources.publisher: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
sources.locator: Frizzleds belong to class F GPCRs and share an extracellular cysteine-rich domain, a hydrophilic linker, a seven-transmembrane domain and an intracellular C-terminal region. The contributions of the 7TM domain to signal transduction are called contentious; Frizzleds show limited direct G-protein coupling, leading to debates over whether they should be classified strictly as GPCRs or as a broader family with hybrid functionalities. ZNRF3 and RNF43 ubiquitinate Frizzleds for lysosomal degradation.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY), no version stated on the article page; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

sources.title: Tales from the crypt: intestinal niche signals in tissue renewal, plasticity and cancer
sources.locator: In the crypt the Wnt pathway synergizes with Notch to sustain undifferentiated proliferative stem and progenitor cells; Notch-blocking antibodies converted Lgr5+ stem cells to secretory cells and depleted stem cells with Wnt upregulation, rescued by repressing Wnt, which the authors say suggests opposing and interconnected activities. BMP represses Wnt in an opposing gradient along the crypt-villus axis, highest at the luminal surface; antagonists come from mesenchyme. Mouse small intestine.
